edges.description: Senescent cells are apoptosis-resistant, so once the rate at which they arise outpaces immune clearance they accumulate in the bone microenvironment.
edges.target: Senescent Cell Accumulation in the Bone Microenvironment

edges.description: Senescent-cell conditioned medium enhances osteoclast-progenitor survival and osteoclastogenesis, converging on the same resorption-favouring state that estrogen loss produces by a different route.
Clearing senescent cells lowers resorption while maintaining trabecular and raising cortical formation, which is the remodeling imbalance running in reverse.
edges.source: Senescent Cell Accumulation in the Bone Microenvironment

edges.description: Diverting the shared precursor away from the osteoblast lineage reduces the formation side of the remodeling unit, so the imbalance is reached without any increase in osteoclast activity.
edges.source: Marrow Stromal Lineage Shift Toward Adipogenesis

edges.description: Estrogen restrains osteoclastogenesis largely by holding down RANKL relative to osteoprotegerin, so its withdrawal releases that brake directly. This is why bone loss accelerates sharply at menopause rather than gradually with age.
Tobacco shifts bone turnover toward loss on top of whatever else is driving remodelling, lowering attained bone mass. The responsible constituents and steps are not established in the cited source.
Therapeutic glucocorticoids suppress osteoblast function and lifespan while prolonging osteoclast survival, tipping remodelling toward resorption. It is the commonest secondary cause of the disease.
Unloading removes the mechanical signal that normally restrains resorption, and this entry carries a node specifically for it. Notably the loss is not fully reversible on return to gravity.
The line was established specifically to make osteocyte mechanotransduction and osteocyte-osteoblast-osteoclast communication testable in vitro.
edges.limitations: Murine, immortalized by SV40 large T antigen, and cultured on collagen-coated plastic rather than embedded in mineralized matrix, so the lacuno-canalicular geometry that carries the mechanical signal in vivo is absent. It does not model aging.

edges.description: Provides a readout of sclerostin production and its hormonal regulation, the formation-side brake in the remodeling unit.
edges.limitations: Murine and conditionally immortalized. It reconstructs a differentiation trajectory, not a remodeling unit - there are no osteoclasts in it, so the balance this entry models cannot be observed directly.

edges.description: Reconstitutes both arms of the remodeling unit in human cells, with osteoblastic mineralization and osteoclastic resorption in the same construct.
edges.limitations: The imbalance is imposed by adding myeloma plasma cells, not by estrogen withdrawal or aging, so the disease-relevant driver is a different one. It is short-term (weeks), has no vasculature, no marrow adipocyte compartment, and no mechanical loading, so neither the senescence nor the marrow-lineage node in this entry can be studied in it.
edges.source: 3D bone organoid with coupled osteoblast-osteoclast remodeling

edges.description: Reproduces the estrogen-deficiency route into accelerated remodeling, and the effect is estrogen-reversible, which establishes the mechanism rather than merely the phenotype.
edges.limitations: Captures the estrogen-withdrawal arm only. It says nothing about the senescence and marrow-lineage arms of this entry, which are age-driven and present in both sexes.

edges.description: Trabecular bone volume falls and stays low, so the structural endpoint is reproduced, but the driving turnover signal is not sustained.
edges.limitations: Over a 12-month study the cancellous turnover indices return to sham control values while trabecular bone volume remains low, so the model decouples the mechanism from the deficit at exactly the durations the guidance recommends. It also lacks intracortical Haversian remodeling entirely, so cortical porosity cannot be studied in it.

edges.description: Clearing roughly 30% of senescent cells in old mice raises bone mass, microarchitecture and strength; the same treatment in 12-month-old mice changes nothing, which is the specificity control.
edges.limitations: Murine, and the transgene is not a therapy. The mouse skeleton lacks osteonal cortical remodeling, so the cortical arm of the result does not transfer directly. The human phase 2 senolytic trial did not reproduce the resorption effect at its primary endpoint - see the discussions section.
edges.target: Senescent Cell Accumulation in the Bone Microenvironment

edges.description: Aged mice lose cancellous bone, thin their cortices and gain cortical porosity as humans do, and the histologic cause is shared - resorption cavities that osteoblasts fail to refill.
edges.limitations: The murine skeleton keeps growing slowly after puberty and has no osteonal remodeling of cortical bone, so the human intracortical remodeling compartment has no counterpart in it. Cortical findings therefore arise through a different structural process than the one they are taken to model.
edges.source: Aged mouse skeleton as a model of human age-related bone loss

edges.description: Turns the structural deterioration this node describes into a mechanical quantity that prospectively predicts hip fracture, and the load-to-strength ratio stays predictive after adjustment for areal BMD.
edges.limitations: Resolves geometry and density at CT scale, so it does not represent trabecular connectivity or cortical porosity directly, and it says nothing about the cellular mechanisms upstream. Validated here in older men; the cohort is not the population most affected.
edges.source: QCT-based finite element model of the proximal femur

edges.description: Reproduces a single remodeling cycle, self-sustaining cycling, and unstable runaway remodeling from one parameter set, and identifies autocrine regulation of osteoclasts as the parameter that decides which regime the system occupies.
edges.limitations: A single-site abstraction with lumped parameters and no spatial structure, no osteocyte compartment, and no aging or estrogen axis, so it cannot represent the senescence or marrow-lineage nodes in this entry. Its pathological regime was matched to Paget disease rather than to osteoporosis.
edges.source: Bone cell population dynamics model of the remodeling unit

nodes.description: A human bone organoid built by letting marrow stromal cell-derived osteoblasts mineralize an endosteal-like matrix for 21 days, then adding marrow macrophage-derived osteoclasts to restore resorption. It is the closest available non-animal system to the coupled remodeling unit this entry models, and it reports the same CTX-1 resorption marker used clinically.
nodes.id: 3D bone organoid with coupled osteoblast-osteoclast remodeling

nodes.description: A suicide transgene that lets p16INK4a-expressing senescent cells be killed on demand with AP20187. Applied to 20-22-month-old mice with bone loss already established, it is an interventional test of whether senescent cells cause age-related bone loss rather than merely accompany it.

The background model underneath most murine bone aging work. Recorded explicitly because its divergences from the human skeleton are the reason several results in this entry are held at moderate rather than high fidelity.
nodes.id: Aged mouse skeleton as a model of human age-related bone loss

nodes.description: Increased osteoclast-mediated bone resorption relative to osteoblast- mediated bone formation leads to net bone loss. This imbalance accelerates with aging and estrogen deficiency.

computational_models.description: Reproduces a single remodeling cycle, self-sustaining cycling, and unstable runaway remodeling from one parameter set, and identifies autocrine regulation of osteoclasts as the parameter that decides which regime the system occupies.
computational_models.name: Bone cell population dynamics model of the remodeling unit

evidence.reference_title: Aromatase activity and bone loss.
evidence.snippet: aromatase activity and estrogen production are necessary for longitudinal bone growth, attainment of peak bone mass, the pubertal growth spurt, epiphyseal closure, and normal bone remodeling in young individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Aromatase deficiency, a rare syndrome: case report.
evidence.snippet: Estrogen deficiency can induce delayed epiphyseal closure, eunuchoid body habitus, osteopenia, and osteoporosis in both genders.

nodes.description: A differential-equation model of autocrine and paracrine signalling between osteoblast and osteoclast lineages at a single remodeling site, solving for cell population dynamics and the resulting change in bone mass. It is the formal counterpart of this entry's Bone Remodeling Imbalance node.

evidence.reference_title: Mathematical model predicts a critical role for osteoclast autocrine regulation in the control of bone remodeling.
evidence.snippet: Parametric analysis demonstrated that the mode of dynamic behavior in the system depends strongly on the regulation of osteoclasts by autocrine factors, such as transforming growth factor beta.

evidence.reference_title: Denosumab for prevention of fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.
evidence.snippet: denosumab reduced the risk of new radiographic vertebral fracture, with a cumulative incidence of 2.3% in the denosumab group, versus 7.2% in the placebo group (risk ratio, 0.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.26 to 0.41; P<0.001)

evidence.reference_title: Vertebral Fractures After Discontinuation of Denosumab: A Post Hoc Analysis of the Randomized Placebo-Controlled FREEDOM Trial and Its Extension.
evidence.snippet: the vertebral fracture rate increased from 1.2 per 100 participant-years during the on-treatment period to 7.1, similar to participants who received and then discontinued placebo

evidence.reference_title: Aromatase activity and bone loss.
evidence.snippet: extraglandular aromatization of circulating androgen precursors is the major source of estrogen not only in men (since only 15% of circulating estradiol is released directly by the testis) but also in women after the menopause.

evidence.reference_title: Estrogen and bone: insights from estrogen-resistant, aromatase-deficient, and normal men.
evidence.snippet: studies in these unusual patients have stimulated research on defining the role of estrogen in regulating bone metabolism in normal adult and aging men, providing further insights into estrogen regulation of bone metabolism not only in men, but also in women.

evidence.reference_title: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis: an update.
evidence.snippet: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis is the most common secondary cause of osteoporosis and the resulting fractures cause significant morbidity.

nodes.description: A conditionally immortalized line that traverses the whole osteoblast-to-late-osteocyte transition in culture and expresses SOST/sclerostin under PTH and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 control. That makes it the accessible in vitro system for the sclerostin axis this entry targets pharmacologically with romosozumab.

Murine long bone osteocyte line immortalized under an osteocalcin promoter. It made the osteocyte experimentally accessible, which matters here because the osteocyte is the cell this entry's senescence and mechanosensing nodes both run through.

Osteoblasts and marrow adipocytes derive from a shared mesenchymal precursor, and with age that precursor is allocated increasingly to the adipogenic rather than the osteogenic fate. Marrow adipose volume rises with age and is higher again in osteoporosis at matched age, and it is inversely correlated with trabecular bone volume - a decline in the regenerative output of the stromal compartment rather than a change in resorption.
nodes.id: Marrow Stromal Lineage Shift Toward Adipogenesis

evidence.reference_title: Adipocyte tissue volume in bone marrow is increased with aging and in patients with osteoporosis.
evidence.snippet: There was an age-related inverse correlation between BV/TV and AV/TV (r = -0.58, P < 0.001).

evidence.reference_title: Adipocyte tissue volume in bone marrow is increased with aging and in patients with osteoporosis.
evidence.snippet: Compared with age-matched controls, patients with osteoporosis exhibited an increased AV/TV (P < 0.05) and decreased BV/TV (P < 0.05)

nodes.description: Loss of trabecular connectivity and cortical thinning compromises bone strength beyond what BMD alone indicates. Leads to fragility fractures with minimal trauma. Spaceflight accelerates this process, with incomplete microarchitectural recovery even one year post-flight.

evidence.snippet: nine of 17 astronauts did not fully recover tibia total BMD after 12-months

evidence.snippet: bone structural quality (e.g., trabecular microarchitecture) is diminished and the quality of bone material is reduced via impaired tissue mineralization, maturation, and maintenance (e.g., mediated by osteocytes)

evidence.reference_title: One-month spaceflight compromises the bone microstructure, tissue-level mechanical properties, osteocyte survival and lacunae volume in mature mice skeletons.
evidence.snippet: osteocyte death was evidenced along with a smaller and more spherical shape of the osteocyte lacunae because of lacunar mineralization

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers.
evidence.snippet: Bone loss in space travelers is a major challenge for long-duration space exploration.

evidence.snippet: nine of 17 astronauts did not fully recover tibia total BMD after 12-months

evidence.reference_title: Pre-flight exercise and bone metabolism predict unloading-induced bone loss due to spaceflight.
evidence.snippet: Increases in training volume predicted preservation of tibia bone strength and trabecular vBMD and thickness

evidence.reference_title: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight.
evidence.snippet: Wild type mice lost significant muscle and bone mass during the 33 d spent in microgravity

nodes.description: Spaceflight induces a rapid and sustained increase in osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Astronauts lose approximately 0.8% of bone mass per month in weight-bearing lower limb sites, with bone resorption markers plateauing at 113% above pre-flight levels within days of entering microgravity.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers.
evidence.snippet: Bone loss in space travelers is a major challenge for long-duration space exploration.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers.
evidence.snippet: microgravity-induced bone loss is a significant and unresolved health risk for space travelers

nodes.description: Microgravity removes gravitational mechanical loading, impairing osteocyte mechanotransduction. Osteocytes sense mechanical strain via the lacuno-canalicular network and regulate bone remodeling accordingly. In microgravity, loss of fluid shear stress and mechanical stimulation leads to downregulation of key osteocytic genes and impaired osteocyte differentiation.

evidence.reference_title: Global transcriptomic analysis of a murine osteocytic cell line subjected to spaceflight.
evidence.snippet: µG impairs the differentiation of osteocytes, consistent with prior osteoblast spaceflight experiments, which resulted in the downregulation of key osteocytic genes

evidence.reference_title: Skeletal changes during and after spaceflight.
evidence.snippet: clear parallels exist between the effects of spaceflight, periods of immobilization and ageing, with possibly irreversible features

experimental_models.description: The line was established specifically to make osteocyte mechanotransduction and osteocyte-osteoblast-osteoclast communication testable in vitro.
experimental_models.name: MLO-Y4 osteocyte-like cell line

nodes.description: With advancing age, osteocytes - the long-lived, terminally differentiated, non-dividing cells that orchestrate remodeling - upregulate p16INK4a and acquire a senescence-associated secretory phenotype. Osteocytes and myeloid cells are the two bone-resident populations that predominantly develop the SASP, and the secretome impairs osteoblast mineralization while enhancing osteoclast-progenitor survival. This is the aging arm of the entry: it is distinct from estrogen deficiency and operates in both sexes.

biological_processes: SASP cytokine production by senescent osteocytes
Inflammatory response in the bone microenvironment

evidence.reference_title: Identification of Senescent Cells in the Bone Microenvironment.
evidence.snippet: senescent myeloid cells and senescent osteocytes predominantly develop the SASP

evidence.reference_title: Identification of Senescent Cells in the Bone Microenvironment.
evidence.snippet: revealed significantly more senescent osteocytes in old compared with young bone cortices (11% versus 2%, p < 0.001)

evidence.reference_title: Identification of Senescent Cells in the Bone Microenvironment.
evidence.snippet: Corresponding with the age-associated accumulation of senescent osteocytes was significantly higher expression of multiple SASP markers in osteocytes from old versus young mice

nodes.description: Bilateral ovariectomy in the rat produces acute estrogen withdrawal, a surge in cancellous bone turnover, and net trabecular bone loss at the proximal tibia, distal femur and lumbar vertebrae. The 1994 FDA preclinical guidance names it as the rodent species for evaluating agents intended to treat or prevent postmenopausal osteoporosis, which makes it the regulatory reference model rather than merely a common one.

A patient-specific structural model built from a quantitative CT scan of the hip, solving for femoral strength and for the ratio of the load a fall would impose to the strength available to resist it. It is the computational counterpart of this entry's claim that microarchitecture and geometry carry fracture risk that areal BMD alone does not.
nodes.id: QCT-based finite element model of the proximal femur

evidence.reference_title: Finite element analysis of the proximal femur and hip fracture risk in older men.
evidence.snippet: These results provide insight into hip fracture etiology and demonstrate the ability of FE-based biomechanical analysis of QCT scans to prospectively predict hip fractures in men.

nodes.description: Increased RANKL and decreased osteoprotegerin (OPG) ratio promotes osteoclast differentiation and activation. Estrogen normally suppresses RANKL and increases OPG. Microgravity further exacerbates this imbalance by directly increasing the osteoblast RANKL/OPG ratio.

animal_models.description: Reproduces the estrogen-deficiency route into accelerated remodeling, and the effect is estrogen-reversible, which establishes the mechanism rather than merely the phenotype.
animal_models.name: Ovariectomized rat

evidence.reference_title: Role of the IL-23/IL-17 Pathway in Rheumatic Diseases: An Overview.
evidence.snippet: The differentiation of osteoclasts is induced significantly in the presence of IL-17 either directly (207), or indirectly, through upregulation of RANKL.

evidence.reference_title: Aromatase activity and bone loss.
evidence.snippet: with aging, individual differences in aromatase activity and thus in estrogen levels may significantly affect bone loss and fracture risk in both genders.

evidence.reference_title: Modeled microgravity stimulates osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption by increasing osteoblast RANKL/OPG ratio.
evidence.snippet: microgravity is capable to indirectly stimulate osteoclast formation and activity by regulating osteoblast secretion of crucial regulatory factors such as RANKL and OPG

evidence.reference_title: Osteoprotegerin is an effective countermeasure for spaceflight-induced bone loss in mice.
evidence.snippet: SF/VEH mice had lower BV/TV vs. GC/VEH mice, while SF/OPG-Fc mice had greater BV/TV than SF/VEH or GC/VEH

nodes.description: Senescent cells accumulate across multiple bone-resident lineages with age. The burden is causal rather than a bystander marker: clearing roughly 30% of p16-positive cells in aged mice, genetically or pharmacologically, yields higher bone mass, better microarchitecture and greater strength, and does so only in old animals.
nodes.id: Senescent Cell Accumulation in the Bone Microenvironment

animal_models.description: Clearing roughly 30% of senescent cells in old mice raises bone mass, microarchitecture and strength; the same treatment in 12-month-old mice changes nothing, which is the specificity control.
animal_models.genotype: INK-ATTAC transgenic (inducible caspase 8 under the p16INK4a promoter)
animal_models.name: Aged INK-ATTAC senescent-cell clearance mouse

evidence.reference_title: Targeting cellular senescence prevents age-related bone loss in mice.
evidence.snippet: these data establish a causal role for senescent cells in bone loss with aging, and demonstrate that targeting these cells has both anti-resorptive and anabolic effects on bone

evidence.reference_title: The Effect of Tobacco Smoking on Bone Mass: An Overview of Pathophysiologic Mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: tobacco smoking causes an imbalance in bone turnover, leading to lower bone mass and making bone vulnerable to osteoporosis and fracture
